Hi Lara — great to connect. Appreciate the usage breakdown. High-level answers below; I attached a short cheatsheet and a sample commit proposal to make this concrete.

Quick summary:
- Hosted API supports both pure pay-as-you-go and committed monthly/annual tiers. Commits give blended per-token discounts and are the primary lever for predictable unit cost.
- Model tiers: we price "standard" models at the baseline per-token rate and "premium" models at a defined surcharge (typically 1.5–2x baseline depending on model family and context window).
- Embeddings: charged per-embedding unit (not token), with unit definitions varying by model; we provide an embeddings-to-token rough conversion for comparison.

For a ~100M token/month footprint we commonly structure offers as:
- 12-month commit: 15–25% off baseline per-token rates (higher discounts for larger committed spend)
- 24-month commit: additional 5% uplift on top of the 12-month discount for multi-year certainty
- Premium model surcharge: applied to requests routed to premium models; bundle options available if you want a share of traffic on premium variants

Next steps: can you share expected split of calls routed to embeddings vs chat (approx %)? Also: timeline for contract/PO and whether Acme prefers monthly billing or quarterly invoices for committed spend.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-cheatsheet.pdf, redwood-commit-proposal-ACME-2026.pdf

If helpful, I can loop in Lauren from Sales Ops to draft a formal quote once we have the usage split and preferred term. Available for a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Fwd: Pricing for high-volume hosted API usage — model tiers & commit options

Vanessa / Lauren — forwarding Lara's ask. Quick internal notes and proposed structure before we send a formal quote:

Context: ACME expects ~100M tokens/month (60% embeddings, 40% chat). They want guidance on commit sizing and model selection (standard vs premium). They asked for year-1 and year-2 examples.

Proposed commercial approach:
- Offer a tiered commit with blended rate:
  - Tier A (>=20M tokens/month): baseline rate R_base
  - Tier B (>=50M tokens/month): R_base * 0.85 (15% off)
  - Tier C (>=100M tokens/month): R_base * 0.75 (25% off)
- Premium model surcharge: +60% of R_base for premium chat; embed models priced at R_embed = R_base * 0.5 (we bill per-embedding unit).
- Volume crediting: unused committed tokens in a month roll into a 90-day buffer; true-ups quarterly.
- Term: 12-month with optional 24-month at +5% discount on blended rate.

Example (illustrative only):
- If they commit 100M tokens/month at Tier C in year 1, blended per-token = R_base * 0.75. If 60% embeddings, estimate effective embedding unit price equals R_base * 0.375 (after embedding multiplier). If they use premium chat for 30% of traffic, premium surcharge applies to those tokens.

Discount flexibility: we can bump to 28–30% off for a strategic reference customer or if they commit to a 24-month term with specific SLA targets. Need leadership approval for anything beyond 30% off.

Actions: Lauren, can you draft the formal quote (line items for baseline tokens, embedding units, premium surcharge, term discounts, and DocuSign-ready SOW)? Vanessa, can you take point on the commercial call and push for a 12- or 24-month commit (we should prefer 24-month for better ARR visibility).

Thanks — will keep the thread light externally until we have the draft.

— Marcus

Highlights (summary):

- Option B — 24-month commitment (100M tokens/month): 30% off baseline per-token rate; same embedding and premium multipliers; 90-day unused token buffer and quarterly true-up.
- Billing: monthly invoices against committed tokens with quarterly true-ups.
- SLAs: Standard hosted SLA (99.9% uptime) included; upgraded SLA available as add-on.
